authority.legal_name: NYC Ferry (New York City Economic Development Corporation)
authority.geography_type: a major estuary and harbour (the East River, Upper/Lower Bay and ocean-facing Rockaway) around the five boroughs
authority.home_waters_label: New York Harbor and the East River

mandate.summary: NYC Ferry is the citywide public ferry system run by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC). Launched in 2017, it carries millions of riders a year on six routes and ~25 landings linking the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island at a subway-equivalent fare.
current_priorities: Operate the six-route citywide network (East River, South Brooklyn, Astoria, Rockaway-Soundview, St. George, Governors Island) at an integrated public fare
Optimize and extend the network - the December 2025 route changes added the St. George (Staten Island) route to Manhattan and Brooklyn
Decarbonize the fleet in line with NYC's climate goals (Local Law 97 / OneNYC carbon-neutral 2050)
Improve reliability and landing accessibility across the boroughs

policy_targets.vision: OneNYC / carbon-neutral 2050; citywide ferry as an equitable public transit mode
policy_targets.decarb_note: NYC's climate plan targets carbon neutrality by 2050; the ferry fleet is a diesel layer that a zero-emission foiling tier directly decarbonizes.
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling tier is the obvious fleet-renewal path for NYC Ferry - faster, quieter, low-wake hops on the East River and harbour, decarbonizing a system the city already subsidizes as public transit.

precedent.headline: NYC Ferry already runs a six-route, ~25-landing citywide public network at a subway-equivalent fare.
precedent.network: East River, South Brooklyn, Astoria, Rockaway-Soundview, St. George and Governors Island routes - landings from Throgs Neck and Soundview in the Bronx to the Rockaways, St. George and Bay Ridge.
precedent.note: Ferry is an established public-transit mode in New York, run by NYCEDC. Navier renews and decarbonizes the fleet on the busy commuter water.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined foiling upgrade to a public ferry network NYC already runs as transit. Foiling hulls are faster and far lower-wake - valuable on the wake-sensitive, current-swept East River - and open frequencies and longer harbour hops (Rockaway, Soundview, St. George) the displacement fleet runs slowly.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/wharves/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public-ferry stops; new/committed stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The East River spine - Pier 11 to East 34th; the busiest commuter water, where low-wake foiling is most valuable.
Short, very high-frequency cross-river hop between DUMBO and Lower Manhattan.
Lower Manhattan to the Rockaways across the harbour - a long open-water run where a fast foiling boat sharply cuts the trip.
East 34th up to Soundview in the Bronx - a long East River / upper-harbour commuter leg.
Lower Manhattan to St. George, Staten Island - the new 2025 route across the Upper Bay.
Pier 11 to Brooklyn Bridge Park / Atlantic Ave on the South Brooklyn line.
South Brooklyn waterfront line via Red Hook and Sunset Park to Bay Ridge.
Pier 11 up the East River to Astoria via the Brooklyn Navy Yard and Roosevelt Island.

regional_links.note: NYC Ferry is a domestic, within-city network. There is no cross-border or long-range domestic marine corridor in scope; ocean services beyond the harbour (e.g. toward New Jersey or Long Island) are out of the core proposal.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: The East River is a tidal strait with very strong reversing currents, peaking at Hell Gate; routing and speed must account for current set, and foiling control must manage the standing chop.
New York Harbor carries dense commercial, tug-and-barge and Staten Island Ferry traffic under Coast Guard VTS; respect the traffic-separation scheme and cross lanes cleanly.
Governors Island / Red Hook legs cross Buttermilk Channel; St. George legs cross the Upper Bay toward the Narrows - both busy, current-swept and wake-sensitive.
The Rockaway run crosses open Lower Bay / ocean-influenced water past Coney Island; route the marked channel and manage swell.
Many landings sit on narrow piers with kayak and recreational traffic; geofence no-foil, low-wake zones at every landing approach.
All harbour bridges have ample navigable clearance for ferries; keep geometry in the marked channels under the East River bridges.
